function: Joint active beamforming (BS precoder) and passive beamforming (STAR-RIS phase shifts and amplitudes) to maximize the user sum rate, p. 1, 8.
system: BS with 16 antennas (ULA), K single-antenna users, L=4 distributed energy-splitting STAR-RISs of M elements (UPA), direct link blocked; frequency band not stated, p. 3, 9.
method: Heterogeneous graph neural network (BHGNN) of FCNN blocks with message passing; unsupervised training on negative sum-rate loss with Adam, Lagrangian dual for QoS, p. 7-8.
data_channel: Custom Rician fading simulator, path loss 32.6+36.7log10(d) dB, ULA/UPA steering vectors; 50,000 generated channel realizations, 45,000 training and 5,000 testing, p. 9.
test_conditions: Trained at (Nt,L,M,K)=(16,4,4,8) on users in one rectangle; tested with other numbers of users, STAR-RISs, elements (Table II) and other user-location areas (Fig. 6), p. 9, 11.
baselines: Non-learned: AO-SCA, AO-SCA-EXH, AO-SCA with one centralized STAR-RIS, random phase shift. Learned: HomoGNN [18], HetGNN [21], CNN [35], p. 9-10.
metrics: Sum rate (also relative to AO-SCA), QoS constraint violation degree, average CPU running time, p. 10-12.
complexity: Order O(LMNt^2+KNt^2+TNt) for online inference, p. 9; CPU time 25.7-43.3 ms versus 177.4-1271.7 ms for AO-SCA, Table III, p. 12.
q1_support: p. 9: "follow the Rician fading channel models" with its own path loss 32.6 + 36.7 log10(d) dB; custom simulator, no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 9: "the BHGNN is trained for the setting of (Nt, L, M, K) = (16, 4, 4, 8), and is tested with different settings"; p. 11: "most of the user locations are unseen in the testing phase".
q3_support: p. 9: "HomoGNN: A homogeneous GNN design that is originally proposed for a single RIS-aided system in [18]", plus HetGNN [21], CNN [35], AO-SCA and random phase shift; p. 11: "the CNN, HomoGNN, and HetGNN models underperform compared to BHGNN" in sum rate (Fig. 5).
q4_support: p. 9: "the proposed HBGNN exhibits lower complexity compared to the AO-based SCA algorithm" after giving O(LMNt2 + KNt2 + T Nt); p. 12: Table III lists average running times of AO-SCA and BHGNN.
q5_support: p. 9: "50,000 channel realizations are generated as dataset"; the dataset is self-generated and no code or data link is given, and no public channel dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Included, area 3 (joint BS precoder and STAR-RIS configuration with a learned GNN). The sentence on p. 12 says BHGNN is 'slower' than AO-SCA, but Table III shows it faster (apparent typo). Frequency band not stated anywhere.
